skills.name: Showing inequalities on the number line

note.text:
The solutions of an inequality can be shown on a number line.
• A circle marks the end number. A filled circle (●) means the end number is included (≤ or ≥). An open circle (○) means it is not included (< or >).
• A thick line with an arrow shows all the other solutions: to the right for > and ≥, to the left for < and ≤.
x > 2: open circle at 2, arrow to the right. x ≤ −1: filled circle at −1, arrow to the left.
To show the solutions of 2x + 1 ≥ 7, solve first (x ≥ 3), then draw a filled circle at 3 and an arrow to the right.

worked_example.problem: Solve {poly([a, 'x'], [b, ''])} < {a * k + b} and describe how to show the solutions on a number line.
steps: The sign < does not include {k}: draw an open circle at {k}.
Less than means to the left: draw a thick line from the circle with an arrow to the left.
worked_example.answer: x < {k}: open circle at {k}, arrow to the left.

cards.idea: A filled circle means the end number is included (≤, ≥). An open circle means it is not (<, >).

check.prompt: In the drawing of {ineq('x', op, k)} on a number line, what is the circle at {k} like?

misconceptions.explain: {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'The sign ' + op + ' includes ' + fmt(k) + ', so the circle is filled.' : 'The sign ' + op + ' does not include ' + fmt(k) + ', so the circle is open.'}

solution: {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'The sign ' + op + ' includes ' + fmt(k) : 'The sign ' + op + ' does not include ' + fmt(k)}.

cards.idea: The arrow points to the solutions: right for > and ≥, left for < and ≤.
To show the solutions of an inequality, solve it first, then draw the circle and the arrow.
example: {poly([a, 'x'], [b, ''])} ≥ {a * k + b} gives x ≥ {k}: filled circle at {k}, arrow to the right.

questions.prompt: Which inequality is shown on the number line?

misconceptions.explain: Look at the arrow: it points to the {op == '>' || op == '≥' ? 'right' : 'left'}.
Look at the circle: it is {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'filled' : 'open'}.
Look at the arrow and at the circle.

solution: The circle at {k} is {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'filled, so ' + fmt(k) + ' is included' : 'open, so ' + fmt(k) + ' is not included'}.
The arrow points to the {op == '>' || op == '≥' ? 'right (greater numbers)' : 'left (smaller numbers)'}.

questions.prompt: The number line shows the solutions of an inequality. Which whole numbers from {k - 3} to {k + 3} are solutions?

distractors.text: {solutionsIn(k - 3, k + 3, op == '<' || op == '>' ? looseOp(op) : strictOp(op), k)}

misconceptions.explain: Look at the circle at {k}: it is {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'filled, so ' + fmt(k) + ' is a solution' : 'open, so ' + fmt(k) + ' is not a solution'}.
The arrow points to the {op == '>' || op == '≥' ? 'right' : 'left'}: those are the solutions.

solution: From {k - 3} to {k + 3}, these numbers satisfy it: {answer}.

questions.prompt: The number line shows the solutions of one of these inequalities. Which one?

misconceptions.explain: That inequality solves to {ineq('x', flipOp(op), k)}: the arrow would point the other way.
That inequality solves to {ineq('x', op, k + 1)}: the circle would be at {k + 1}.
Look at the circle: {op == '≤' || op == '≥' ? 'filled, so the sign must include ' + fmt(k) : 'open, so the sign must not include ' + fmt(k)}.

solution: Solve {answer}: {b < 0 ? 'add ' + fmt(-b) : 'subtract ' + fmt(b)} and divide by {a} to get {ineq('x', op, k)}.
